findings.title: deleteCache does not check delegation credential ownership
findings.body: The handler only looks up prisma.credential with userId filter. For delegation credentials (which may not have a direct userId or are shared), this check could incorrectly allow or deny access, or miss validating that the credential actually belongs to the acting user in multi-tenant/org scenarios. Other handlers in this codebase use more thorough credential ownership checks (including org/team credentials). This bypass could allow deleting cache for credentials not truly owned by the user if credential.userId semantics differ (e.g., shared/team credentials).

findings.title: N+1 free pattern but new repository instance ignores credential type correctness
findings.body: getCacheStatusByCredentialIds is called with all credentialIds including non-Google-calendar integrations (Office365, etc.) and in-memory delegation credentials whose credentialId may be negative (per isInMemoryDelegationCredential checks elsewhere in CalendarCacheRepository). Passing negative/in-memory credential IDs into the groupBy query is harmless but wasteful, and more importantly it does not filter by integration type, so the resulting cacheUpdatedAt map is computed for all credential types though it's only meaningful for Google Calendar. This doesn't match the pattern elsewhere in the code (e.g. assertCalendarHasDbCredential) which explicitly guards against invalid credential ids being used in cache lookups.

findings.title: updatedAt added as @updatedAt but migration lacks backfill/default consistency check
findings.body: The Prisma field uses @default(now()) @updatedAt, meaning Prisma manages it automatically on every write (including raw upsert calls in calendar-cache.repository.ts that don't explicitly set updatedAt). This is fine for Prisma Client writes, but any raw SQL inserts/updates to CalendarCache (e.g. via migrations or external scripts) that don't go through Prisma Client will not get updatedAt refreshed automatically, since @updatedAt is implemented at Prisma Client/query level, not DB level. If any other code path writes to CalendarCache via raw queries, cache status reporting will be stale/incorrect.

findings.title: Hardcoded locale in date formatting ignores user's language settings
findings.body: new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...) hardcodes the locale instead of using the user's configured locale from useLocale(). This will show reversed/incorrect-looking date formats for non-English users, inconsistent with the rest of the app's localization support that was added in this PR (new i18n strings).

findings.title: interpolation option improperly placed inside t() call
findings.body: The `interpolation: { escapeValue: false }` option is passed inside the same object as the `timestamp` interpolation value for `t("cache_last_updated", {...})`. react-i18next expects interpolation options to be passed separately (as part of i18next options), not mixed with variables; here it will be treated as an extra named variable, not as an actual interpolation config, so it has no effect and could show up unexpectedly if the translation string references it.

findings.title: Unconditional updateManyByCredentialId call after every fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache regardless of cache miss/hit
findings.body: fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache now unconditionally calls SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId for all selected calendars under the credential, bumping SelectedCalendar.updatedAt even when this method is invoked as part of routine operations (e.g., unwatchCalendar's call to repopulate cache for remaining calendars). This adds an extra DB write on every fetch cycle, which, combined with CalendarCache being queried heavily, could add non-trivial write load, and the PR description itself notes this field isn't actually surfaced in the UI (cacheUpdatedAt from CalendarCache is used instead), making this update likely unnecessary overhead.
